Briefing for 16 November 2026

Short items for 16 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

Study · More technical

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra helps with a physics proof

OpenAI has launched a science blog. In its first guest post, UCSB physicist Nathaniel Craig says GPT-6 Astra led the detailed proof for his candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model.

Source: OpenAI

Everyday tool

Claude Enterprise merges chat and Cowork

Enterprise teams now use one Claude for quick questions and longer tasks. When work needs code or files, it continues in a cloud environment run by Anthropic, and admins control access by role.

Source: Anthropic

Everyday tool

Apple tests health chatbot answers in a new study

With OpenEvidence, Apple launched a US study app that answers health questions using clinical journals. It aims for up to 200,000 iPhone users over more than 12 months, and the data is not used for model training.

Source: TechCrunch

AI agents

Google opens its research agent teams in Antigravity

Google Research says /teamwork agent teams helped experts solve open problems in math, chemistry and kernel optimization. Developers can now use the same tools in Antigravity.

Source: Google Research

New model

Haru-4B listens and speaks at the same time

Higurashi released open weights for Haru-4B, a speech model you can interrupt mid-sentence like on a phone call. It reaches about 65 ms latency on a MacBook and is a base model meant for research.

Source: Higurashi

Everyday tool

ElevenLabs tests an app for meeting notes and dictation

ElevenAI records meetings, answers questions across past calls and turns speech into clean text in any app, in more than 90 languages. It is still in preview with early-access sign-up.

Source: TechCrunch

Everyday tool

Cheap AI API keys let a middleman read everything

heise bought a key worth $50 in model credit for €2.20. Real Anthropic models answered, but via an opaque gateway whose operator can read and alter every prompt, according to a security expert.

Source: heise online

In the background

Report: Jensen Huang discusses a return to Nvidia

The Financial Times reports that the former Nvidia CEO has discussed a comeback with close allies. A public letter backing his return has over 150,000 signatures, though many are hard to verify.

Source: The Verge

Be brave. Get smart.
